evaluations.note: 30 on the reference machine since the neighbour lists are exact (2026-09-30; 16 before). BFGS reaches the upper bound RCUT2B = 6.0 at eval 9 (the best, 1.031156e-01), and from eval 13 on its line search re-evaluates the clamped bound; its sufficient-decrease test there depends on the sign of the ~1e-13 relative re-evaluation noise of the warm-started lattice relaxation. On the reference machine it never passes and the run continues to MAXEVAL (30, status COMPLETED); with the hot_a0 start 1 ulp lower it passes and BFGS ends after 17 evaluations (as example 05's run with the same search does after 16). So the count is not pinned (evals_tol 14: 16..30, see tolerance_rationale); best loss, components and RCUT2B do not depend on it.

tolerance_rationale: Best loss, components and RCUT2B are pinned at the default tolerances. The evaluation count is not deterministic across machines: the optimum is on the clamped bound RCUT2B = 6.0 (eval 9), and whether DLIB:BFGS's line search accepts a re-evaluation there depends on the sign of a ~1e-13 relative, rounding-level drift of the warm-started lattice relaxation. With exact neighbour lists (2026-09-30) the run goes on re-evaluating the bound to MAXEVAL = 30 on the reference machine (3 repeated runs identical), and a 1-ulp lower hot_a0 start makes it stop after 17 (it stopped after 16 before); evals_tol 14 accepts 16..30. The status is COMPLETED either way.
